articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 22, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (September 22, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, September 22, 2026.
Indian women’s cricket team brought in the first gold medal for the country at the ongoing Asian Games 2026 as companies line up to go public, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured news
Deoria MP Shashank Mani Tripathi on the 2026 NEET crisis, India's growth story and entrepreneurship
A paper leak, a resignation and a rocket launch, how one MP connects examinations, growth and enterprise into a single argument.
Meet the solar didis turning sunlight into a source of livelihood in rural Bihar
In Bihar’s Muzaffarpur district, solar didis use clean energy to bring water to farms, build incomes, and gain financial independence.
Today’s key developments
Women's cricket team gives India first gold of 2026 Asian Games
The Indian women's cricket team reasserted its continental dominance by clinching a second successive gold medal at the Asian Games, thrashing familiar foes Sri Lanka by 147 runs on Tuesday. The Harmanpreet Kaur-led side's gold was India's first of the ongoing edition and was shaped by a brilliant batting performance that left Sri Lanka chasing a record target of 217.
Snapdeal parent firm AceVector's IPO to open on September 25
AceVector plans to raise Rs 420 crore through the IPO and has priced its shares in the range of Rs 30-32.
Spinny files confidential IPO papers, eyes upto Rs 3,000 Cr
In August, Spinny’s parent company Valuedrive Technologies converted from a private limited company into a public limited company.
Captain Fresh revenue crosses Rs 5,000 Cr in FY26; co targets Rs 10,000 Cr in FY27
The packaged seafood company saw adjusted EBITDA rise by 173% in FY26 as it remained net profit positive for the second consecutive year.
Funding news
Definedge raises Rs 22 crore in Pre-Series A round
Pune-based fintech and brokerage firm Definedge Securities Broking has raised Rs 22 crore in a Pre-Series A funding round, taking its total capital raised to Rs 30 crore. The round saw participation from existing investors Nitin Agarwal and D Prasad, along with new investors Anant Jain and Sachin Kasera. The company plans to deploy the funds towards infrastructure, low-latency execution, product development, marketing and distribution, and AI and automation capabilities.
Definedge is targeting Rs 5,000 crore in assets under management through its Momentify platform over the next 24 months, having already crossed ₹1,000 crore. It will also expand Algostra, its no-code retail algorithmic trading platform, and scale its investor education ecosystem, Gurukul. The company said its overall user base has grown 125% in 14 months.
Protein Pantry raises Rs 9 cr led by Sharrp Ventures
Protein Pantry, a high-protein frozen food brand has raised Rs 9 crore in a seed round funding. The round was led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from Peercheque, Consumer Collective by Atrium and Indian Silicon Valley Capital, alongside angels including Varun Alagh (Honasa), Rishubh Satiya (Plix), Avnish Anand (CaratLane), Arush Chopra (Just Herbs), Saurabh Munjal (Lahori Zeera), Signal Ventures and others.
The capital will primarily be deployed into setting up and scaling the brand's manufacturing unit, alongside continued investment in R&D and supply chain. The balance goes into marketing and working capital. Protein Pantry is also extending its ranges with new formats. Over the next 12 to 24 months, the company is targeting availability across all major Indian cities via D2C and quick commerce and continued expansion of its protein range across categories. Since launching in November 2025, Protein Pantry has gone live direct-to-consumer across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Jaipur, and on quick commerce via Blinkit, FirstClub and Flipkart Minutes across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
Demoverse raises $600K led by Lumikai
AI-powered co-creation platform Demoverse has raised $600,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by Lumikai, which invested $500,000 through its Pixels programme. The round also saw participation from UAE-based investor-operator Marlan and angel investors. Demoverse enables consumer brands to involve customers in product creation before production begins. Brands post concepts and design directions, while consumers use AI to reshape and refine them. The community then evaluates and votes on designs, generating product direction and demand signals before manufacturing commitments.
Contributors whose ideas influence winning products can earn royalties when those products are commercialised. The company is initially focusing on fashion and plans to expand into beauty, consumer packaged goods and other categories. Founded by Akshay Mehta, Demoverse has already conducted trials with Indian consumer brands and plans to convert these partnerships into paid campaigns.
YNOS receives Rs 2.12 Cr investment from Gyan Circle Ventures
YNOS, a technology platform providing information and fundraising analytics for India’s startup ecosystem, has received an investment of Rs 2.12 crore from Category-I venture capital fund Gyan Circle Ventures. The funding will support YNOS in expanding its technology capabilities and widening its reach among entrepreneurs and investors. The platform aggregates information on startups, founders, incubators, angel investors, venture capital firms, corporates, government agencies and banks. It provides tools for valuation estimation, investor identification, competition analysis and ecosystem mapping.
As of September 2026, YNOS covers more than 3.42 lakh startups, 5.92 lakh founders, 14,667 angel investors, 6,310 VCs, 1,458 incubators, 137 government schemes and 1,096 banks and financial institutions. More than 875 startups have used YNOS for fundraising, collectively raising around ₹4,000 crore.
TimBuckDo raises bridge round ahead of Series A
Bengaluru-based on-demand convenience platform TimBuckDo has raised a bridge round backed by Srinath Setty, Co-founder and CEO of Hosachiguru, through family office Trasa Ventures, and Adarsh Narahari, Founder and Managing Director of Primus Senior Living. The company has not disclosed the size or valuation of the round. The funding will support technology development, expansion of its verified student workforce, deeper presence in existing markets and expansion of service categories ahead of a planned Series A round.
TimBuckDo operates a network of educated college students, known as “Doers”, who provide flexible, on-demand services including elder companionship, pet care, child support, errands and assistance to home businesses. The company aims to build an organised marketplace connecting verified student talent with households and businesses while enabling students to earn flexibly alongside their education.
Other news
Delvitech to invest up to $30M in Bengaluru facility
Swiss AI-native Automated Optical Inspection company Delvitech has announced plans to establish a manufacturing and technology facility in Bengaluru with an initial investment of $10 million and an overall investment of $25-30 million. The 65,000-square-foot facility is expected to become operational in the first quarter of calendar 2027 and could create 500-800 jobs over the next five years.
The plant will integrate precision machining, metrology and equipment integration, alongside mechanical, electrical, optical, software and control systems. It will also support engineering and R&D activities, product demonstrations and customer trials. Delvitech said the investment reflects its long-term commitment to India’s electronics manufacturing sector. The company showcased its Horus, Aton and Horus Dual Lane inspection solutions at productronica India 2026 in Bengaluru, highlighting AI-driven approaches to electronics quality inspection and manufacturing efficiency.
Simplilearn partners with Karmayogi Bharat for AI skilling
Digital skills training company Simplilearn has partnered with Karmayogi Bharat under the Government of India’s Mission Karmayogi to provide AI and digital upskilling programmes for public sector professionals. The programmes will be hosted on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and cover foundational and advanced topics including artificial intelligence, data analytics, cloud computing, cybersecurity, Generative AI and project management.
The partnership is designed to provide government officials with flexible, self-paced learning that can be integrated into their daily workflows. Karmayogi Bharat said the initiative will help strengthen capabilities across roles and support digitally enabled public administration. Simplilearn said its AI-first learning architecture and SkillUp platform will support continuous learning at scale. The company operates globally across 150-plus countries and offers more than 1,500 live classes each month, reaching over 15 million learners.
Integra Robotics secures Indian patent for remote robotic manipulation
Integra Robotics, a unit of Social Hardware International, has secured Indian Patent No. 597459 for a system enabling remote manipulation of robotic platforms through a virtual reality interface. The patented technology allows human operators to control robots remotely using VR, camera-based depth information and gesture gloves that provide electronic feedback. The architecture integrates VR headsets, motion sensors, infrared gesture gloves, processing modules, network routers and robotic manipulators. Human movements are translated into robotic commands using Bio-Inverse Kinematics.
The technology is designed for applications where direct human intervention may be difficult or hazardous, including industrial operations, inspection, defence and disaster response. Integra Robotics has also filed two additional patent applications covering platform-independent robotic manipulation and operator-intent transformation. The company said the technology strengthens its intellectual property portfolio in advanced robotics and immersive teleoperation.
Masters’ Union Demo Day sees Rs 60 Cr in funding commitments
Masters’ Union Ventures held its first Demo Day in Bengaluru, with 25 student-led startups securing soft-funding commitments of nearly Rs 60 crore within an hour of their pitches. The event brought together more than 65 venture capital firms and angel investors, with participating startups spanning AI, climate and space technology, biotechnology, consumer businesses and advanced manufacturing.
Sanyark, Saubha Aerial Systems and CarbonM were among the startups receiving significant investor interest. The event also featured an AI hackathon conducted with Qualcomm Developer and the launch of a guidebook titled ‘Don’t Start a Stupid Startup’. About 60% of participating startups were built through Masters’ Union’s Venture Initiation Programme. The programme and related initiatives have supported more than 80 student startups, while 50 VIP-incubated ventures have collectively raised over ₹320 crore.
Matters.AI and Cockroach Labs integrate for data security
Bengaluru-based Matters.AI and New York-based Cockroach Labs have announced an integration that identifies personal and regulated data within CockroachDB deployments at the column level and maps it to users, roles and privileges with access. The solution scans databases, tables and columns using 38 personally identifiable information detectors covering eight regulatory jurisdictions, along with payment card data, protected health information and secrets stored in free-text fields.
The system produces a live access map showing which accounts can access regulated data and where data may be stored in inappropriate jurisdictions. Classification and privilege analysis take place inside customers’ infrastructure, while raw records and sampled values are not transmitted. The companies said the integration can support compliance with frameworks including India’s DPDP Act, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001 and SOC 2.
Stratbeans expands AI-led workforce learning solutions
AI-led enterprise learning company Stratbeans is helping manufacturing organisations improve workforce skills, training coverage and employee performance through digital learning and AI-powered knowledge solutions. Its Ask AI platform enables employees to obtain answers to work-related questions using approved standard operating procedures, policies, manuals and training documents. The company combines digital learning, AI-powered assessments, multilingual learning and intelligent knowledge support. Stratbeans said training coverage at one organisation increased from 20% to 85%, while platform usage reached 80% and the average assessment pass rate stood at 88%.
Its solutions also include Proctored Evaluation for assessments and SIM Studio, which allows employees to practise workplace scenarios through roleplay and receive AI-generated feedback. The company said Ask AI can also help managers identify frequently searched topics and areas where additional training or documentation may be required.
Fynd brings virtual eyewear try-on to Vision Express India
AI-native retail technology company Fynd has partnered with Vision Express India to introduce immersive eyewear shopping through its GlamAR 3D virtual try-on and augmented reality solution. Integrated into the Vision Express website, the technology allows customers to virtually try different eyewear styles. Fynd converted more than 1,000 existing two-dimensional eyewear product assets into production-ready 3D models and brought them live for virtual try-on.
Since launch, the experience has recorded more than 3,900 virtual try-on interactions. Black Square Frames for Men emerged as the most tried-on frame, with more than 400 interactions, while the top 11 frames accounted for nearly 34% of total try-on activity. The next phase will focus on measuring conversions and optimising the online shopping experience using customer try-on behaviour to inform eyewear merchandising.
TalentGum receives STEM.org accreditation and recognition
Online extracurricular learning platform TalentGum has received the STEM.org Accredited Educational Experience Trustmark from STEM.org Educational Research. The company has also been named among the Top 5% of “Best in STEM” brands in a separate recognition. TalentGum said the accreditation provides independent validation of its learning proposition as it expands its extracurricular and skill-based programmes for children. The STEM.org accreditation evaluates educational experiences against a framework focused on interdisciplinary learning and real-world application.
TalentGum offers live courses covering areas including coding, artificial intelligence and machine learning, chess, arts, dance and public speaking. The platform is used by parents across more than 70 countries. The company said the recognition reinforces its focus on helping children develop transferable skills, critical thinking, communication and practical problem-solving through interactive learning experiences.
Atom Risk Advisory secures global insurance broking licence
Atom Risk Advisory, an Indian insurance intermediary operating since 2019, has announced that its group entity has secured a global insurance broking licence. The licence will enable the company to enter international insurance markets and offer cross-border insurance solutions to clients. Atom said its global offering will cover areas including Universal Life Insurance, Private Placement Life Insurance, Keyman Insurance and bespoke legacy solutions. The company plans to strengthen partnerships with international insurers and reinsurers, expand specialist teams and invest in technology-driven risk advisory capabilities.
The move comes as Indian enterprises and family offices expand their international footprint and face increasingly complex risk, wealth and succession planning requirements. Atom Risk Advisory specialises in life and health insurance, family protection, corporate insurance, succession planning and legacy solutions. It is part of Atom Financial Services Group, which also has capabilities in wealth management, investment banking and estate planning.
MyBranch expands South India workspace network
Flexible workspace and managed office provider MyBranch has expanded its South India presence to a 50,000-square-foot footprint across 16 centres in 14 cities spanning Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
Its network covers Bengaluru, Coimbatore, Guntur, Hanamkonda, Hubballi, Hyderabad, Madurai, Mangaluru, Rajahmundry, Salem, Tirupati, Vellore, Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, with another large office planned in Chennai. According to JLL data cited by the company, Bengaluru and Hyderabad together accounted for 49.7% of India’s net office absorption in H1 2026, while flexible workspace represented 27% of gross office leasing. MyBranch said its network is designed to support enterprises, MNCs, GCCs, startups and growing businesses establishing regional offices or satellite teams. Founded in 2016, the company now has more than 80 locations across 75-plus cities.
Lxme partners with Shiprocket to expand UPI reach
Financial platform Lxme has partnered with Shiprocket to expand the reach of Lxme UPI across India’s direct-to-consumer commerce ecosystem. The integration is already live across Shiprocket’s Fastrr merchant ecosystem, allowing merchants to offer Lxme UPI without additional integrations. Eligible transactions can also earn customers Digital Gold, linking everyday payments with wealth-building. The partnership is expected to expand Lxme UPI’s availability across hundreds of merchant websites spanning categories such as beauty, grocery and D2C commerce.
Lxme said the initiative supports its strategy of encouraging women to participate in wealth creation through everyday financial transactions. The partnership is non-exclusive, allowing Lxme to continue expanding its merchant network. Shiprocket said the collaboration aims to add greater value to the checkout experience for consumers and D2C brands.
Olyv appoints Ravi Sharma as Chief Financial Officer
Digital lending platform Olyv has appointed Ravi Sharma as its Chief Financial Officer as the company enters its next phase of growth. Sharma brings more than 17 years of experience across financial services and has previously served as CFO at Finova Capital. During his tenure at Finova, he helped lead financial initiatives, close five equity funding rounds and onboard more than 50 lending partners. At Olyv, Sharma will oversee financial strategy, capital planning, risk governance and long-term value creation as the company expands its portfolio of financial products and services.
HCLTech selected by M Group for IT transformation
HCLTech has been selected by UK and Ireland-based essential infrastructure services provider M Group to modernise and transform its IT operations across more than 200 locations. Under the engagement, HCLTech will deploy AI-led managed services covering infrastructure and end-user operations, using its AI Force service transformation platform. The programme will seek to streamline M Group’s IT environment, improve resilience and establish a scalable digital foundation.
The transformation will support M Group’s businesses across water, energy, technology and communications, transport, defence, industrial and public sectors. M Group said the partnership will help strengthen IT reliability and scalability while supporting innovation and sustainable growth. HCLTech said its experience in complex, multi-site environments would support M Group’s technology transformation. HCLTech has more than 223,000 employees across 60 countries, with revenues of $14.8 billion for the 12 months ended June 2026.
Zurich Kotak launches digital insurance proposition for SMEs
Zurich Kotak General Insurance has launched a digital-first insurance proposition aimed at simplifying business protection for small and medium enterprises. Powered by Zurich’s technology platform, Zurich Edge, the solution brings quotation, purchasing, servicing, referrals and underwriting together through a single interface.
Its Business Secure Plus proposition offers bundled protection across areas including fire and special perils, burglary, electronic equipment, fidelity guarantee, directors and officers liability, employee compensation, money and machinery breakdown. Zurich Kotak said the platform enables businesses to obtain customised coverage and premiums based on their risk profiles, with policy issuance possible within minutes. The insurer said SMEs’ contribution to India’s GDP and their employment role underline the need for easier access to insurance. Zurich Kotak is a 70:30 joint venture between Zurich Insurance Group and Kotak Mahindra Bank.
Ubalance Naturals unveils ‘The Forest Within’ brand identity
Ayurvedic wellness company Ubalance Naturals has introduced a new brand identity, ‘The Forest Within’, across its portfolio of nine products and 18 SKUs. The company also announced an ambition to reach ₹100 crore in revenue by FY30. The new identity reflects the company’s philosophy that wellbeing is shaped by interconnected bodily systems rather than isolated functions. Ubalance Naturals said it sees opportunities in India’s growing Ayurvedic wellness market, with industry estimates cited by the company placing the market at around $11.9 billion in 2025 and projecting it to reach $43.2 billion by 2034. The company combines Ayurvedic principles with contemporary scientific understanding and offers formulations addressing areas including energy, stress response, digestive and liver wellness, metabolic health, respiratory wellness and mobility. The new identity will extend across packaging, digital platforms, e-commerce and retail touchpoints.
QNu Labs launches QShield 2.0 for quantum security assessment
Quantum security company QNu Labs has launched QShield 2.0, the platform powering its National Cryptographic Assessment & Assurance Framework, at its 10th anniversary event in Bengaluru. The framework is designed to help organisations identify and assess their cryptographic assets as they prepare for the transition to post-quantum security. QNu Labs said the platform operates through three processes: Discover, Assess and Assure. QShield 2.0 includes modules covering quantum entropy, quantum-readiness risk assessment, quantum PKI, quantum vault and AI security.
The launch comes after a Department of Science and Technology task force report in February 2026 recommended that critical infrastructure sectors begin formal post-quantum cryptography implementation by 2027. The company said early deployment accounts include banks and security depositories. QNu Labs has been incubated at IIT Madras Research Park and has received support from India’s National Quantum Mission.
Apurva.ai expands LENS into cross-organisational knowledge platform
Apurva.ai has announced a new platform model for Apurva LENS, expanding it from an organisation-level knowledge tool into a platform designed to support learning and collaboration across the wider development ecosystem. The AI-enabled platform helps funders, governments, NGOs and change leaders connect research, evaluations, programme experience and community voices. Apurva.ai said LENS has helped surface more than half a million voices and perspectives from the Global South. Under the new model, organisations can share selected knowledge while retaining control over private information.
The platform has been used by organisations including SELCO Foundation and Resilience Action Network Africa to organise and analyse institutional knowledge, community dialogues and research. In Brazil, Museu da Pessoa has used LENS to explore patterns across an archive of life stories. The platform aims to connect fragmented knowledge while retaining local context and human judgement.
Privacy by Design 2026 brings startups and investors together in Bengaluru
DPDP Zone’s Privacy by Design 2026 summit brought together 350 attendees, including 250 founders and 35 investors and fund representatives, in Bengaluru. The event focused on privacy, cybersecurity, responsible AI and digital trust as businesses prepare for India’s Digital Personal Data Protection framework. A separate invite-only Demo Session enabled 15 startups to pitch directly to investors. Participating funds included Bessemer Venture Partners, Kalaari Capital, Blume Ventures, Chiratae Ventures, Inflection Point Ventures, Campus Fund and Venture Catalysts. The programme featured technical sessions and panel discussions covering privacy by design, responsible AI, cybersecurity, founder trust and governance in fundraising. Organisers said the event was held eight weeks before provisions governing Consent Managers under the DPDP Rules were scheduled to take effect on November 13, 2026. Substantive provisions of the Act are scheduled for enforcement from May 13, 2027.
KEDGE launches 18-month MBA programme in India
European business school KEDGE has announced the launch of its MBA programme in India in association with keeplearning. The 18-month programme will combine face-to-face teaching, asynchronous learning and a 14-day in-person immersion, allowing working professionals to pursue the qualification without leaving their careers. Participants will receive an MBA credential directly from KEDGE and access to its alumni network of more than 90,000 graduates. The curriculum covers strategy, finance, marketing, operations, leadership, innovation, international management and sustainable enterprise. It also includes India-focused modules on Generative AI for business operations and responsible AI governance.
The programme features simulations, masterclasses, leadership workshops, coaching and a capstone project based on a live business challenge. The inaugural cohort will be limited, with selection involving an academic assessment, mini-case presentation and interview.
Globe Moving appoints Smartya Majumder as Country Head – Sales
Workforce and workplace mobility company Globe Moving has appointed Smartya Majumder as Country Head – Sales. He brings more than 19 years of experience across logistics and telecom, with previous leadership roles at TNT India, Samsung Electronics, Vivo Mobile India, DHL–Blue Dart Express and DTDC. Before joining Globe Moving, Majumder served as Vice President and National Sales and Marketing Head at Trackon. In his new role, he will oversee sales strategy, revenue growth, business development and customer-focused mobility solutions.

articles.title: Microsoft anuncia demissões no Xbox e pode fechar estúdio • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft anuncia demissões no Xbox e pode fechar estúdio
Halo Studios perdeu 268 funcionários, enquanto o estúdio de Hellblade entrou em consulta sobre possível fechamento.
A Microsoft anunciou a demissão de 268 funcionários do Xbox nesta terça-feira (22/09). Os empregados estavam alocados no Halo Studios. A mudança integra “a reestruturação mais significativa da história do Xbox”, segundo o comunicado assinado pelo executivo Matt Booty.
Além disso, de acordo com Booty, “dois acordos separados” para a venda da Ninja Theory, estúdio responsável por Hellblade: Senua’s Sacrifice, “não se concretizaram”. Como resultado, a Microsoft está agora em um período de consulta para que ele feche, a menos que encontre outro comprador, como lembrou o The Verge.
Os cortes fazem parte de um plano de eliminar 3.200 vagas relacionadas ao Xbox até o fim de junho de 2027. Há dois meses, a Microsoft cortou cerca de 1.600 funcionários e abriu mão do controle de quatro estúdios, atingindo equipes de diferentes produtoras ligadas à empresa. Entre as equipes afetadas estavam Bethesda, ZeniMax Online e id Software.
A nova CEO do Xbox, Asha Sharma, busca melhorar as margens de lucro da divisão e concentrar investimentos nas maiores franquias da Microsoft, como The Elder Scrolls e Fallout. Apesar disso, os cortes anteriores também alcançaram equipes ligadas diretamente às duas séries, além da id Software, conhecida por Doom e Quake.
Os novos ajustes dão continuidade a uma reformulação iniciada meses atrás. Em junho, o Tecnoblog adiantou que a Microsoft preparava demissões em massa e mudanças no modelo de negócios do Xbox, incluindo redução de despesas e revisão dos investimentos em diferentes áreas.
Na época, a divisão enfrentava pressão para controlar os custos após anos de investimentos em conteúdo, infraestrutura e hardware. A estratégia traçada sob o comando de Sharma também previa uma revisão do desenvolvimento de jogos e maior foco nas franquias consideradas importantes para o Xbox.
A reorganização ficou mais evidente em julho. Além das demissões, a Microsoft começou a reverter parte das aquisições realizadas durante a gestão anterior, liderada por Phil Spencer, que havia ampliado o número de estúdios internos para fortalecer o catálogo do Xbox Game Pass.
Em comunicado divulgado durante a primeira rodada de cortes, Sharma afirmou que as mudanças buscavam dar à divisão “mais foco, mais disciplina e mais clareza”. A executiva também disse que a Microsoft manteria o nível de investimentos no Xbox, apesar da redução do quadro de funcionários e da saída de alguns estúdios.

articles.title: iOS 27.2 may include an anti-snatch AutoLock feature for iPhones, aimed at thwarting thieves — and more new features have been spotted in the latest beta
articles.text:
iOS 27.2 beta 2 includes new details of an iPhone anti-snatching feature, plus a first look at more changes coming to Apple Music, Shortcuts, and more
A thief-thwarting upgrade and various app improvements
- The second iOS 27.2 developer beta has landed, and code points to several upcoming features
- These include an anti-snatching tool, so the phone locks itself if it detects a sharp grab or when disconnected from your Apple Watch
- There are changes hinted at for Shortcuts, Apple Music, and CarPlay Ultra too
The second iOS 27.2 developer beta has now landed, and while on the face of it this doesn’t look much different to the first beta, behind the scenes there’s quite a lot of new stuff to find.
Digging into the code, 9to5Mac has found more details of an anti-snatching feature that we’ve previously reported on. This as-yet-unannounced feature is apparently called ‘AutoLock’ internally at Apple, and is designed to lock your phone if a thief grabs it.
It sounds similar then to Android’s Theft Detection Lock, and the code in this beta suggests that it would use various signals to tell whether an iPhone has been stolen, such as a sharp acceleration (which could happen when a phone is first snatched), loss of connectivity to a paired Apple Watch, a paired Apple Watch being unreachable, prolonged loss of network activity, or the device remaining unlocked for a certain period of time.
Any of these things could trigger an iPhone to automatically lock itself, but there are also references to safeguards aimed at preventing false positives. These include things like successful biometric authentication, and certain innocent app activities that could otherwise be signs of theft.
Other hidden features
On top of this, as spotted by X user @itspdfu (via 9to5Mac) iOS 27.2 beta 2 also includes code for a new album release countdown in Apple Music, and for the ability to support actions from third-party apps in Shortcuts new ‘Describe a Shortcut’ tool. So you’ll be able to include third-party apps in shortcuts built using natural language, rather than having to use the old shortcut builder.
Finally, @aaronp613 has found evidence that CarPlay Ultra will soon offer a ‘Drive Mode Theme’, allowing you to change things like the gauge style and color. Though right now CarPlay Ultra is only available on Aston Martin vehicles, so this might be of limited usefulness.
Of course there’s the usual caveat with all this that while Apple is seemingly working on these features, we can’t be sure of if or when they’ll actually launch. But they all sound like worthwhile upgrades, so hopefully they will roll out — and soon.

articles.title: ChatGPT débarque dans Microsoft Word, et vous n’avez même pas besoin de payer
articles.text:
OpenAI pousse un peu plus loin l’intégration de ChatGPT aux outils bureautiques de Microsoft. Dans Word, l’assistant travaille désormais directement à partir du document ouvert, même si plusieurs fonctions du chatbot manquent encore à l’appel.
Près de deux ans après son arrivée sur Windows, ChatGPT empiète un peu plus sur les terres de Copilot et débarque officiellement dans Microsoft Word. OpenAI vient en effet d’étendre au traitement de texte son complément déjà proposé dans Excel et PowerPoint, désormais accessible à tous les comptes, y compris gratuits. L’assistant peut ainsi s’appuyer sur le document ouvert pour le résumer, le corriger ou retravailler un passage, sans multiplier les allers-retours entre applications.
Des fonctions bien intégrées, mais encore quelques absents
Pour en profiter, il faudra d’abord récupérer le complément depuis le Microsoft Marketplace, directement dans Word via Accueil > Compléments, tout à droite du ruban. Une fois le module installé et connecté au compte OpenAI, ChatGPT s’ouvre dans un volet latéral, à côté du document en cours.
Il peut alors résumer l’ensemble du texte, corriger ou reformuler une sélection, transformer quelques consignes en brouillon, mais également reprendre les titres, la structure ou la mise en forme du document.
Cette intégration ne reprend toutefois pas tout ce que ChatGPT connaît déjà de vous. Les échanges lancés dans Word n’apparaissent pas dans l’historique du chatbot, tandis que les informations enregistrées en mémoire et les compétences sauvegardées sur le compte ne sont pas accessibles depuis le complément. L’usage du module est par ailleurs décompté du quota associé à l’offre ChatGPT souscrite et peut, selon la formule, puiser dans une enveloppe partagée avec Codex et d’autres fonctions premium.
Même distinction pour les plugins, qui ne sont pas utilisables depuis Word pour le moment. Les services reliés au compte ChatGPT, comme Outlook, SharePoint, Google Workspace ou Dropbox, peuvent en revanche fournir au complément les informations dont il a besoin.

articles.title: Microsoft está haciendo limpia y eso tiene una consecuencia: 'Halo' pasa a las manos de Activision-Blizzard
articles.text:
Había rumores sobre una noticia gorda relacionada con despidos en Xbox a lo largo del día de hoy, pero lo que quizá no esperábamos era que esa noticia gorda fuera la confirmación de algo que llevaba un tiempo sonando. Dentro de la gran reestructuración de Xbox, Activision, responsable de 'Call of Duty' entre otras franquicias, pasará a controlar la saga estrella de Xbox: 'Halo'.
Por sí sola, esta noticia ya haría temblar a más de uno, pero no se queda ahí porque 'Sea of Thieves' y 'Age of Empires' pasan, desde hoy, a estar también bajo el paraguas de Activision.
Y no son los únicos cambios.
Halo Studios. Como podemos leer en The Verge, dentro del gran plan de limpieza de Microsoft, la franquicia 'Halo' pasará a depender de Activision-Blizzard. Cuando Bungie, padres de la saga 'Halo' abandonó Microsoft, la gigante estadounidense montó un estudio llamado 343 industries encargado al completo de crear juegos de ese universo. Tras varios tropiezos, renacieron bajo el nombre de Halo Studios, cuyo primer juego fue el 'Halo Campaign Evolved' lanzado este verano.
Desde el mismo momento del lanzamiento, y teniendo en cuenta que Xbox ya estaba en plena reestructuración, los rumores sobre que otro estudio de la empresa pasaría a controlar la franquicia empezaron a florecer, y el único candidato posible es el que ha terminado siendo: Activision.
Un Halo digno. Esa es la intención de Rob Kostich, presidente de Acitivision, quien ha declarado que el objetivo "es claro: hacer el mejor juego de 'Halo', digno de su universo y legado, mientras nos mantenemos fieles a lo que hizo que los jugadores lo amaran en un primer lugar". Son declaraciones audaces, sobre todo cuando su franquicia estrella, 'Call of Duty', una que deberían conocer a la perfección lleva años sin entregar un producto que consiga convencer de pleno a los jugadores.
Kostich continúa comentando que se trata de algo audaz y que ya han comenzado a reunir un equipo especialmente diseñado para la franquicia, con el talento y capacidad para entregar el próximo capítulo de la misma". Eso era, precisamente, 343 industries y Halo Studios, un estudio que falló no tanto por la incapacidad de sus miembros, sino porque tenían una política de contrataciones curiosa en la que había una gran rotación de miembros que salían por la puerta cuando conseguían asentarse.
En el comunicado, afirman que esto no afectará al desarrollo y planes de 'Call of Duty', que al final es una de las gallinas de los huevos de oro de Xbox (por eso la sacaron de Game Pass).
No sólo 'Halo'. Como parte de la maniobra, Activision también pasará a controlar 'Sea of Thieves', con sus desarrolladores, Rare, respondiendo directamente ante Activision. Además, World's Edge, responsables actuales de 'Age of Empires', también pasarán a formar parte de Activision.
Más cambios en estudios principales. Aparte del artículo de The Verge en el que podemos leer el comunicado de Matt Booty, uno de los responsables de Xbox junto a la CEO, Asha Sharma, la compañía estadounidense ha publicado una entrada en el blog de noticias en la que detallan otros cambios dentro de la organización:
- Obsidian, que estaba trabajando en un nuevo 'Fallout', pasará a formar parte de Bethesda.
- Turn 10 (responsables de los 'Forza Motorsport'), que fue desmantelado hace unos meses y puesto en cuarentena, ahora formará parte de Playground Games, el estudio de 'Forza Horizon' y 'Fable'.
- Despidos: en total, 268 personas entre capas de gestión, estudios y Halo Studios como nombre propio.
Ahora sí, cierres. Cuando nos enteramos de la estrategia de Xbox de cerrar el grifo, hablamos de cinco estudios que estaban en peligro. Compulsion y Double Fine consiguieron la autogestión, pero había tres en el aire. Por un lado, Undead Labs y Ninja Theory, en conversaciones para una venta. Por otro, el estudio francés Arkane.
En el blog, Microsoft confirma que Undead Labs ha sido vendido y sigue con el desarrollo de 'State of Decay 3', pero que lamentablemente no se ha encontrado una solución para Ninja Theory y "ahora comenzaremos a consultar con los empleados sobre una propuesta de cierre". Sobre el estudio francés no hay novedades.
Optimismo. Pese a todo, Matt Booty apunta en el comunicado que es el momento de mirar hacia adelante a "uno de los catálogos de juegos más fuertes de nuestra historia". Esto es algo para lo que hay que echar imaginación estando las cosas como están, pero según el directivo, es necesario para "fortalecer las franquicias y juegos a través de menos capas burocráticas".
Con los nuevos despidos, se calcula que desde julio habrían salido de Xbox unas 1.900 personas, pero ya sabemos que falta por comunicar unos 1.300 despidos más a lo largo de los próximos meses. Si ahora mismo ya hay estudios que han cerrado, que han tenido que recomprarse, que apenas pueden operar (id Software) o que han quedado en el chasis y tienen que unirse a otros, ese futuro fuerte del que habla Booty es algo complicado de imaginar.

articles.title: Ça y est, Warner Bros. va passer sous l'égide de Paramount : les détails d'un deal historique (et très contesté)
articles.text:
Après des semaines de bataille juridique, le rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery par Paramount est enfin débloqué. Ce deal à plus de 100 milliards de dollars doit faire naître un nouveau mastodonte hollywoodien, mais est aussi loin de faire l’unanimité.
En février dernier, Paramount et Warner Bros. Discovery s’accordaient sur une acquisition à hauteur de 110 milliards de dollars au terme d’une bataille acharnée avec Netflix, qui lorgnait également sur le studio historique. Mais au mois de juillet, douze États américains, menés par la Californie, ont attaqué cette fusion en justice.
Leur crainte : voir Paramount concentrer un pouvoir bien trop important sur la distribution de films, les grosses productions et les chaînes câblées. De quoi suspendre l’opération, une décision qui vient justement d’être levée.
Les engagements de Paramount
Ce lundi 21 septembre, Rob Bonta, procureur général de Californie, a ainsi annoncé un accord à l’amiable avec Paramount, mettant fin au litige qui bloquait la fusion depuis l’été. Dans une note adressée à ses équipes, le patron du groupe, David Ellison, a lui aussi confirmé avoir obtenu un feu vert complet, avec une finalisation du rachat espérée sous environ deux semaines.
Car Paramount a travaillé dur en coulisses afin d’obtenir gain de cause, et a finalement accepté plusieurs contreparties. La société s’engage, par exemple, à sortir 30 films en salle chaque année pendant deux ans, puis 32 par an pendant les trois années suivantes, dont au moins 20 % de grosses productions à gros budget. Si ces quotas ne sont pas respectés, l’entreprise devra payer une pénalité de 30 millions de dollars par film manquant. Elle disposera alors de six mois supplémentaires pour se mettre en règle, faute de quoi elle devra céder le studio Miramax.
En outre, Paramount promet d’augmenter ses dépenses de production aux États-Unis d’au moins 300 millions de dollars par an pendant cinq ans, et s’interdit de revendre les terrains de ses studios ou de ceux de Warner Bros. Le groupe met également en place un comité chargé de garantir l’indépendance éditoriale de CBS News et de CNN, et négociera séparément les tarifs de ses chaînes câblées et de celles de Warner Bros. Discovery pendant cinq ans. Un accord distinct a par ailleurs été trouvé avec le syndicat des scénaristes américains.

Un rachat hautement politique
Mais les voix s’élèvent déjà. Lina Khan, ancienne présidente de l’autorité américaine de la concurrence sous l’administration Biden, juge la fusion « manifestement illégale ». « Les mesures comportementales échouent systématiquement, et les enjeux sont ici particulièrement importants, car une démocratie forte nécessite des marchés ouverts pour garantir un journalisme de qualité et la liberté d’expression créative », assure-t-elle.
Même son de cloche du côté des associations de défense des médias. Free Press accuse notamment le procureur californien d’avoir renié son engagement à protéger consommateurs et salariés. De son côté, Public Knowledge estime que l’accord ne règle en rien le vrai problème posé par cette fusion : la disparition d’un concurrent.
Car, on le rappelle, cette opération s’inscrit dans un contexte politique tendu. Netflix s’est en effet retiré de la course après avoir compris que l’administration Trump donnait clairement sa préférence à Paramount, dirigée par le fils de Larry Ellison, grand ami du président américain. Il aurait multiplié les gestes envers Washington, notamment la promesse de revoir en profondeur la ligne éditoriale de CNN.
Le financement de l’opération, en partie assuré par des fonds souverains saoudiens, émiratis et qataris, alimente lui aussi les critiques sur l’indépendance réelle du futur groupe.

articles.title: KEONICS turns 50, takes Karnataka’s tech story beyond Bengaluru
articles.text:
KEONICS turns 50, takes Karnataka’s tech story beyond Bengaluru
KEONICS marks 50 years with plans to expand technology infrastructure, AI skilling and digital services across Karnataka.
Karnataka’s technology story began long before the AI boom. As KEONICS marks 50 years, the state-backed technology corporation is looking to take that legacy beyond Bengaluru.
Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation Limited (KEONICS) marked its Golden Jubilee in Bengaluru on September 22, celebrating five decades of work across technology infrastructure, digital services, skilling and electronics.
The celebrations were attended by Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, IT and Biotechnology Minister Priyank Kharge, former Chief Minister Veerappa Moily, KEONICS Chairman Sharath Kumar Bache Gowda and other government and industry representatives.
The event also saw the launch of KEONICS’ new logo, the CLT module and a coffee-table book documenting its five-decade journey. A statue of R K Baliga, the founder of Electronic City and KEONICS’ first Chairman and Managing Director, was also unveiled.
From Electronic City to regional tech hubs
Established in 1976, KEONICS played a foundational role in developing 332 acres of land for Electronic City. Over the years, it has evolved from an electronics promotion agency into a technology partner supporting government departments, businesses and citizens.
Its focus now extends to IT infrastructure, digital government, procurement, skill development and technology services across Karnataka.
KEONICS has more than 130 training centres, which have trained and certified over 1.39 lakh students between FY2019-20 and FY2025-26.
The corporation is also building new technology infrastructure in Shivamogga, Mangaluru and Mysuru, while expanding on existing IT parks in Hubballi, Kalaburagi and Shivamogga.
In Shivamogga, KEONICS is developing a 2.5-acre IT Park Annex Phase II and a larger 36-acre IT SEZ. In Mangaluru, a 3.25-acre IT Park at Blueberry Hill, Derebail is being developed, while a 3.48-acre IT Park is planned in Mysuru.
These projects are intended to create technology, employment and business opportunities outside Bengaluru, with public-private partnership and DFBOT models planned for some developments.
Bringing AI and digital services closer to people
KEONICS is also expanding its role as a technology partner for the government through IT consulting, system integration, infrastructure management, procurement and technical workforce deployment.
Its KEONEXT digital marketplace is designed to streamline government-to-government procurement and service delivery across ICT products, IT services, infrastructure, training and technical resources.
At the same time, the organisation is modernising its skilling programmes and Digital Education platform for students and working professionals.
One of its newer initiatives is the KEO AI PC, a Made-in-Karnataka AI-enabled computing product aimed at making AI tools more accessible to students and learners. The planned rollout covers 2,222 KEO AI PCs across 239 taluks and 31 Model Residential Schools, with on-device AI capabilities designed to support digital learning and AI literacy.
“KEONICS has constantly evolved with the needs of Karnataka,” said Sharath Kumar Bache Gowda, Chairman, KEONICS. “Our focus now is to strengthen technology infrastructure, create opportunities beyond Bengaluru, expand skilling and make emerging technologies more accessible.”
Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said KEONICS had been part of Karnataka’s transformation into a global technology destination and would have a role in ensuring technology infrastructure and opportunities reach more parts of the state.
Priyank Kharge described KEONICS as an important execution arm of Karnataka’s technology ecosystem, covering areas from IT infrastructure and services to skilling, digital governance and emerging technologies.
As KEONICS enters its sixth decade, its next chapter is less about building another Electronic City and more about creating a wider network of technology hubs, skills and digital services across Karnataka.

articles.title: En menos de 100 años, Andalucía ha pasado de ser un gigante de la remolacha azucarera a extinguirla por completo
articles.text:
El 1 de enero de 1899, en el Palacio de los Capitanes Generales de La Habana, el gobernador Jiménez Castellanos tomó la palabra y pronunció la frase que ningún militar español quería pronunciar: "en cumplimiento del Tratado de París [...] cesa de existir en Cuba la soberanía española". Arriaron las banderas, marcharon hacia el puerto y se volvieron para la península.
Mirando a Granada. Aquello produjo un impacto descomunal en la España de la época que se haría sentir a lo largo de las décadas. Pero si hay algún sitio al que ese impacto lo cambió de forma radical, ese sitio es Granada. Amplias zonas de las provincias de Córdoba, Sevilla y Cádiz; pero, sobre todo, la vega de Granada.
Buena pare de la modernización urbana de la ciudad y, especialmente, la construcción de la Gran Vía de Colón se pagó con el dinero de algo que se perdió en Cuba: el azúcar.
¿Azúcar? Al perder el suministro preferente del azúcar de las 'posesiones de Ultramar', España se vio obligada a autoabastecerse. Aquello provocó una auténtica fiebre remolachera en Andalucía que supuso una revolución agrícola e industrial. Muchas fortunas (industriales y financieros) y muchas infraestructuras que han marcado el desarrollo agrario del sur de España nacieron de ahí.
A principios del siglo XX, Andalucía sembraba más de 50.000 hectáreas de remolacha. En 2017 quedaban 7.600, con un aforo de 672.000 toneladas. Este año 2026, ya no queda ninguna. La remolacha azucarera ha desaparecido oficialmente de la región.
Un final agridulce. La explicación, como suele pasar, tiene que ver con el dinero. En diciembre de 2023 el azúcar blanco se pagaba a 856 euros la tonelada. En enero de 2026, a 563. Las previsiones nos dicen que bajará hasta los 425 euros. Esa caída del 35% en menos de dos años tiene consecuencias prácticas (y no solo en España): la superficie de remolacha en la UE cayó un 10,6% en estos dos años y cinco fábricas han anunciado su cierre en Europa.
Tampoco es una sorpresa: en Andalucía llevamos años "tonteando" con el fin del cultivo y, de hecho, a día de hoy todo el mundo está a otra cosa: los agricultores plantando girasol como si no hubiera un mañana y la fábrica del Guadalete (gracias a una inversión de 24 millones de euros) procesando caña de azúcar importada.
¿Y por qué es importante todo esto? Antes hablaba de 'tonteo' para referirme al toma y daca entre industria, agricultores y la Junta. Los tres actores, desde hace años, pedía la intervención de Europa. Algo que ha ocurrido este año (con la suspensión de doce meses del régimen de perfeccionamiento activo para el azúcar de caña en bruto), pero que no ha frenado el fin de la remolacha.
Y eso es lo interesante: España lleva décadas siendo un gigante agroalimentario y este caso es un ensayo general de cómo una macroindustria puede desaparecer en un entorno climática y geoestratégicamente tan cambiante como el actual.
Es momento de tomar nota.

articles.title: Renault 5 E-Tech : une autonomie à l’épreuve de la montagne, 409 km engloutis comme si c’était un trajet banal
articles.text:
Renault 5 E-Tech : une autonomie à l’épreuve de la montagne, 409 km engloutis comme si c’était un trajet banal
Sur les routes escarpées des Carpates, la Renault 5 E-Tech a déjoué tous les pronostics en affichant une consommation record sans la moindre recharge. Elle s’est même approchée de l’autonomie WLTP annoncée par le constructeur français.
La citadine électrique n’est pas faite que pour rouler en ville, la Renault 5 E-Tech vient d’ailleurs de le démontrer haut la main. Engagée dans le périple roumain Eurocharge 2026 du média Autocritica, ce modèle tricolore a relié Pitești à Alba Iulia en franchissant les Carpates, et ce, sans pause pour recharger. De quoi confirmer qu’une batterie modeste peut parfaitement encaisser les longs trajets, et donc rassurer les plus sceptiques sur les capacités de la voiture électrique face aux modèles thermiques.
La R5 E-Tech maîtrise ses basiques avec une autonomie à un cheveu du cycle WLTP
Sur un parcours exigeant de 309 kilomètres reliant Pitești à Alba Iulia, la déclinaison Roland Garros de 148 chevaux de la Renault 5 E-Tech s’est frottée à la célèbre Transalpina, un col spectaculaire culminant à 2 145 mètres d’altitude.
Loin d’un test d’éco-conduite aseptisé, l’essai s’est déroulé en conditions réelles, avec deux personnes à bord et des bagages. Tudor Rus, journaliste pour le média roumain Autocritica, résume son enthousiasme : “Petite, vive et amusante par endroits, surtout sur les lacets de la Transalpina. Je ne la cantonnerais pas au cliché de la citadine”.
Le tracé alternait portions à 90 km/h, longues ascensions montagnardes, phases de descente très régénératrices et près de 18 % d’autoroute avalés à 130 km/h. À l’arrivée, le verdict énergétique a dissipé toutes les appréhensions avec une consommation moyenne de seulement 12,7 kWh aux 100 km. La Renault 5 E-Tech a ainsi rallié l’étape d’une seule traite, sans ravitaillement et sans finir à bout de souffle. “Nous sommes arrivés à l’hôtel sans encombre, avec 16 % de batterie et une autonomie restante de 95 kilomètres affichée au compteur”, précise le journaliste.
Rapportée aux 52 kWh de sa batterie, cela donne une autonomie théorique de 409 kilomètres, tutoyant les 410 kilomètres de l’homologation WLTP mixte officielle pour le modèle sorti avant la mise à jour de septembre 2026.
Une performance qui vient balayer d’un revers de main la fameuse angoisse de la panne qui nourrit encore le scepticisme vis-à-vis de l’autonomie dite limitée des voitures électriques. Renault prouve ici qu’une conception sobre et légère surpasse la course aux grosses batteries, permettant à une simple citadine d’avaler les kilomètres et le relief en toute sérénité.

articles.title: Rewes KI-Chatbot: Vom ignorierten Tool zu 5.000 Anfragen im Monat
articles.text:
KI-Akzeptanz: Wie Rewe digital einfach nur den Chatbot umbenannte
Interne IT-Hotlines kommen an ihre Grenzen, je größer ein Unternehmen wird: Anfragen häufen sich, Bearbeitungszeiten steigen und das Vertrauen in den Support bröckelt. Bei der Rewe Group betraf das rund 20.000 Verwaltungsmitarbeitende und ihre Fragen von IT-Störungen bis zu neuer Hard- und Software.
Rewe digital, die IT-Einheit des Konzerns, entwickelte einen eigenen Chatbot: Er beantwortet Fragen direkt aus internen Wissensquellen und legt bei Bedarf automatisch ein Support-Ticket an. Eine Lösung von der Stange war keine Option. Erstens musste der Bot aus Compliance- und Datenschutzgründen dauerhaft in Europa laufen. Zweitens sollte er auf das Wissen zugreifen, das schon in Confluence und SharePoint lag, statt eine komplett neue Wissensbasis aufzubauen.
Technisch überzeugte der Chatbot von Anfang an. Trotzdem nutzte ihn kaum jemand.
KI-Akzeptanz als entscheidender Erfolgsfaktor für IT-Projekte
Damit steht Rewe digital für ein Muster, das laut Bitkom-Studienbericht 2026 viele Unternehmen kennen: Fast jedes dritte Unternehmen (31 Prozent) nennt fehlende Akzeptanz der Beschäftigten als eines der größten Hemmnisse beim KI-Einsatz.
Das zeigte sich hier deutlich: Der Prototyp funktionierte technisch einwandfrei, wirkte aber wie ein trockenes IT-Werkzeug, dem zunächst kaum jemand seine Support-Fragen stellen wollte.
Rebranding als Strategie zur Steigerung der Chatbot-Nutzung
Den Durchbruch brachte am Ende ein Rebranding statt eines technischen Updates: Aus dem nüchternen „Hotline Agent“ wurde „Lumi“ – mit eigenem Namen, Avatar und einer internen Markenkampagne. Warum dieser Schritt so wichtig war und wie Architektur, Compliance-Leitplanken und Rebranding zusammenspielten, zeigt der vollständige Use Case.
Praxiseinblicke in die Architektur und Compliance von Lumi
In diesem t3n PRO Use Case liest du, wie Rewe digital aus einem technisch fertigen, aber ungenutzten Prototypen einen KI-Chatbot machte, der monatlich Tausende IT-Anfragen automatisiert löst:
- Einblick, wie das Rebranding die Nutzungszahlen in Schwung brachte
- Die Architektur dahinter – wie Lumi Treffer nach Relevanz filtert und externes Wissen ausschließt, um Halluzinationen zu vermeiden
- Einblick in die Compliance-Leitplanken, die Rewe digital gemeinsam mit dem Betriebsrat für den KI-Einsatz festgelegt hat

articles.title: Sega nearly killed Sonic before the movies revived the franchise
articles.text:
Through the looking glass: Sonic the Hedgehog has been the face of Sega for well over three decades. In the early 90s, Sonic squared off with Mario for 16-bit console supremacy – and some say he got the better of the bout. But it hasn't always been sunshine and rainbows for the furry blue hedgehog. Indeed, at one point in the not too distant past, Sega almost did away with their iconic mascot.
During a recent interview at the Tokyo Game Show, Sonic boss Takashi Iizuka recalled both the good and bad times. "During the worst times, I was told by the higher-ups that we should cancel the entire franchise. I had to fight within the organization to keep the franchise as long as possible."
A key turning point in the fight to keep Sonic alive came in 2020 with the first live-action movie. If you recall, the first trailer sent the Internet into a tailspin. Viewers were horrified by Sonic's normal-sized eyes, white fur hands, and a mouth full of human-looking teeth. Fortunately, the film's director listened to the criticism and total redesigned the character ahead of launch.
The gamble paid off. Sonic the Hedgehog ended up grossing $320 million at the box office and paved the way for multiple sequels. More importantly, it proved to Sega that the demand for Sonic was alive and well.
The tale highlights just how unstable the entertainment industry can be, and how one project has the potential to make or break a franchise and change the trajectory of history. To date, the Sonic franchise has sold over 1.5 billion copies worldwide.
Imagine how Nintendo's timeline might have looked had the company abandoned Mario following the release of the 1993 live action film. Had the 2020 Sonic film flopped, it's very possible that Nintendo might have thought twice about releasing The Super Mario Bros. Movie in 2023. That animated flick raked in $1.36 billion at the box office.
And who knows how many awesome games and characters we have missed out on because an executive prematurely pulled the plug on a budding franchise. Perhaps in an alternate, parallel timeline, folks are enjoying movies and games we never will.

articles.title: Shuffling the deck chairs: Xbox continues its "reset" with dramatic restructuring
articles.text:
When Xbox announced sweeping layoffs in July as part of a brutal “reset” for the gaming brand, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said part of the pre-existing problem in the gaming unit was “teams, studios, and functions [that] often operate independently, [making it] harder to work toward a shared goal.” Today, the company announced a radical restructuring of its internal studios that is seemingly designed to reduce that “independence” for the teams behind some of gaming’s biggest franchises.
The biggest apparent change is for the Halo franchise, which will now be under the remit of Call of Duty maker Activision. Halo Studios (formerly 343 Industries), which recently released Halo: Campaign Evolved, will remain as just a “small team” to support the player community, Microsoft said, with the remaining staffing roles eliminated as part of 268 newly announced layoffs.
“For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place,” Activision President Rob Kostich said in a statement provided to Kotaku. “It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.”
Activision, which Microsoft officially purchased just under three years ago, will now also take control of venerable studio Rare (Sea of Thieves) and the Age of Empires stewards at World’s Edge.

WhatsApp testa atalho para compartilhar mídias do Instagram e Facebook
Novidade permite acessar mídias das redes da Meta pelo seletor de arquivos.
Uma nova ferramenta em teste pelo WhatsApp deve permitir que os usuários compartilhem fotos e vídeos publicados antes no Instagram e Facebook. A novidade permite que essas mídias sejam enviadas em conversas individuais e em grupos, além de publicá-las no Status, sem precisar alternar entre apps ou baixar os arquivos.
O recurso está sendo liberado gradualmente para testadores das versões beta mais recentes do WhatsApp para Android e iOS. Para usar a integração, é necessário vincular o WhatsApp à Central de Contas da Meta. Por enquanto, não há previsão oficial para a liberação na versão estável do app.
As publicações foram incorporadas ao seletor de mídia do WhatsApp. Ao abrir a galeria para anexar uma foto ou vídeo e acessar a visualização em lista, o usuário passa a encontrar o Instagram e o Facebook entre as opções disponíveis.
Um menu suspenso no topo permite alternar entre as redes vinculadas. As mídias publicadas pelo usuário aparecem em uma grade semelhante à usada para mostrar os arquivos armazenados no celular.
A aproximação entre os aplicativos da Meta vem sendo feita gradualmente. No ano passado, o WhatsApp já havia começado a integrar a Central de Contas para permitir o compartilhamento automático de atualizações do Status nos Stories do Facebook e do Instagram.

articles.title: TerraMaster Announces New U-725 Rackmount NAS Series for Enterprise Storage
articles.text:
Tuesday, September 22nd 2026
	
	
	
	
TerraMaster Announces New U-725 Rackmount NAS Series for Enterprise Storage
TerraMaster, a professional brand specializing in innovative storage products, today announced the launch of four new enterprise rackmount storage servers: the U8-725, U12-725, U12-725 Plus and U16-725 Plus. Designed for medium and large businesses, creative studios, virtualization environments, surveillance deployments and AI-driven workloads, the new lineup combines high-performance processing, flexible storage expansion, high-speed networking and integrated data protection to provide a scalable platform for demanding business environments.
Powered by TerraMaster's TOS 7 AI-native operating system, the new servers are designed to support multiple business-critical workloads from a single platform, including enterprise file services, media collaboration, virtualization, centralized surveillance storage, AI dataset access, backup and disaster recovery. The Ux-725 series is built around Intel Xeon D processors and features ECC memory, NVMe SSD cache acceleration and high-bandwidth networking to provide responsive performance for business applications, virtual machines and large file transfers.The U12-725, is powered by an Intel Xeon D-2712T processor with 16 GB of ECC DDR4 memory, expandable up to 1 TB, allowing organizations to increase available system resources as workloads and business requirements grow. High-speed networking is also built into the platform, with the U12-725 offering up to 50 Gbps of combined network bandwidth through four 10GbE SFP+ ports and two 5GbE RJ45 ports. Support for link aggregation enables businesses to combine network connections to eliminate the implication that link aggregation boosts bandwidth to reach the 50 Gbps bandwidth
The new rackmount servers are also designed to support virtualized environments and AI-focused workloads, providing the storage performance and expansion flexibility required for demanding data applications. Multiple PCIe expansion slots allow organizations to add high-speed networking cards, RAID controllers, AI acceleration hardware and other expansion devices as infrastructure requirements evolve.
Storage capacity can similarly be scaled to suit different environments. The U8-725, U12-725, U12-725 Plus and U16-725 Plus combine multiple drive bays with NVMe cache slots and expansion capabilities, providing businesses with a flexible storage platform that can grow alongside their data requirements. The U12-725 supports up to 12 drive bays, while the larger U16-725 Plus provides 16-bay capacity for organizations managing substantial volumes of business data.Data protection is supported through TerraMaster BBS (Business Backup Suite), which provides a centralized platform for backup, synchronization, snapshots and disaster recovery. The solution enables businesses to protect data across PCs, servers, virtual machines and network storage environments without additional software licensing costs. Built-in snapshot functionality, remote replication and data recovery tools further help protect critical information against accidental deletion, hardware failure and ransomware threats.
All four systems run TerraMaster's latest TOS 7 operating system, bringing together file sharing and collaboration, multi-user access management, virtualization support, centralized backup, cloud synchronization, remote access and monitoring, snapshot protection and AI-ready data management. Together, these capabilities are designed to provide businesses with a single platform for managing, accessing and protecting data across a range of demanding applications.

articles.title: Exclusive: CoreWeave launches Remote Key Encryption to keep customer keys off its cloud - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: CoreWeave launches Remote Key Encryption to keep customer keys off its cloud
Artificial intelligence cloud provider CoreWeave Inc. today unveiled Remote Key Encryption, a service that encrypts customer data sitting on its infrastructure with keys the company itself never holds.
The service takes aim at the key-custody problem that keeps enterprise AI projects parked in security review. Auditors want a named list of everyone able to decrypt sensitive material, and on most clouds the cloud provider is on that list. Model weights and training checkpoints fall under the same rules as any other regulated corporate data, which leaves security teams reconciling an infrastructure choice against obligations written well before the workload existed.
Encryption under the new service runs client-side, inside a customer’s own compute boundary, using keys generated and stored in whatever secrets manager, key management system or hardware security module that customer already operates. No key is imported into a CoreWeave-side key store, so the company holds only ciphertext.
Access to the nodes themselves stays gated behind CoreWeave’s Support Access Management controls. Support engineers at the company cannot reach those nodes without a customer’s express permission, according to the announcement.
Rotation, expiration and revocation run on the customer’s existing schedule and tooling. CoreWeave said the service drives rotation and deletion through that infrastructure rather than standing up a parallel set of controls, and that its approach to key lifecycle management is patent pending. The encryption algorithms underneath are standard ones.
“The fastest path through the loop to production isn’t a new security model,” Andy Manoske, product lead for enterprise and security at CoreWeave, and Paul Friedman, head of security foundations, wrote in a blog post. “It’s making sure our security layer speaks fluently to the one you have already built.”
The same argument drives CoreWeave’s identity work, which landed earlier. CoreWeave IAM handles authentication and authorization across the company’s cloud and federates with enterprise identity providers, Microsoft Corp.’s Entra and Okta Inc. among them, leaving the customer’s own provider as the source of truth. Automated User Provisioning, introduced last November, syncs users and groups continuously, so a hire, a role change or a termination propagates across CoreWeave Kubernetes Service, AI Object Storage and the console without anyone filing a ticket.
Training clusters are a harder case. CoreWeave’s offering for them is SUNK, which packages the open-source job scheduler Slurm for Kubernetes. Slurm keeps a notion of identity all its own, built on POSIX users, groups and accounts, and reconciling those accounts with a corporate directory has traditionally been manual work.
SUNK User Provisioning creates the POSIX user and groups, syncs SSH keys and sets up the Slurm account the moment a federated user turns up in CoreWeave IAM. Add a researcher to a group in Entra or Okta, the company said, and that person can log in to a cluster node inside a minute with the right permissions already set.
Remote Key Encryption enters limited availability later this year, with IBM Corp. as a launch partner. articles.title: Durabook Z14I-DX3 rugged mobile workstation folds three screens into a 9.8 kg chassis — luggable targets military, emergency services, and field professionals
articles.text:
Durabook Z14I-DX3 rugged mobile workstation folds three screens into a 9.8 kg chassis — luggable targets military, emergency services, and field professionals
Rugged computing goes really wide.
Taiwan-based manufacturer Durabook has introduced a highly rugged mobile workstation with not one, not two, but three integrated 14-inch 1080p displays. The Z14I-DX3 comes in a traditional clamshell design with two additional displays attached on either side that fold inwards during transportation. The laptop is MIL-STD-810H and MIL-STD-461G certified and is primarily meant for field professionals including military, public safety and emergency services, engineers, and other industrial operations.
All three displays are DynaVue sunlight-readable touchscreens with capacitive multi-touch and built-in OSD controls. Offering up to 1200 nits of peak brightness, all three can be synchronized or adjusted individually. The displays also support finger, water, glove and stylus inputs, which can be useful depending on the working conditions.
The additional displays increase the overall weight of the machine to a whopping 21.6 lb or 9.8 kgs, significantly heavier than the standard single-screen model at 3.6 kg. And at 5.4" thick (137.5mm) when closed, this system is best understood as a luggable workstation rather than anything resembling a traditional laptop.
The notebook can be configured with Intel’s Meteor Lake Core Ultra 5 or Core Ultra 7 mobile processors with up to 64GB of DDR5-5600 memory. Unusually for a ruggedized system, Durabook also offers several Nvidia discrete GPUs including the RTX A500 AI accelerator, RTX 3500 Ada and RTX 5000 Ada for up to 682 TOPS of AI performance.
The Durabook Z14I-DX3 also offers support for a wide range of connectivity options including Thunderbolt 4, dual RJ-45 Ethernet, two RS-232 serial ports, ExpressCard 54, Nano SIM and eSIM, as well as USB options ranging from USB 3.2 Gen 2 to USB 2.0. Wireless connectivity options include Intel Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, along with optional dedicated GPS, 4G LTE, and 5G connectivity. Durabook touts the use of this connectivity for highly customized application-specific configurations like the addition of joysticks for drone controls.
Given its likely customers, the Z14I-DX3 has several multi-factor authentication options, such as a smart card reader, optional Windows Hello webcam, RFID/NFC reader, and fingerprint scanner. The system also comes with quick-release dual NVMe PCIe SSD drives, allowing users to swap storage drives without requiring any tools. While the main battery is a 6,900mAh unit, the company lists an optional secondary 4,700mAh battery and a 6,700mAh battery for the two additional screens.
There is no information regarding the price, however, customers interested in the rugged mobile workstation can visit Durabook’s official website for a quote.

articles.title: iPhone users are flooding social media with complaints — Apple’s latest iOS move is adding persistent ‘ads’ that can’t be dismissed to users’ devices
articles.text:
‘I wish Apple would just stop that crap': Apple has added persistent ‘ads’ to iOS, and it’s driving users crazy
Way to cheapen the experience, Apple
- iOS users are seeing ‘ads’ for other Apple products on their iPhones
- The banners promote services like iCloud+, Apple Music and AppleCare+
- The messages often can’t be dismissed and stick around for weeks
If you were to ask iOS users how they felt about Apple’s decision to insert ads into Apple Maps, it would quickly become obvious that it was not a popular move. So when iPhone fans discovered that Apple has been inserting prompts for its own products into iOS, the reaction was predictably swift and furious.
The ‘ads’ in question appear in the Settings app in iOS. They can be found near the top of the iPhone’s display and promote several products to the user, including paid-for iCloud+ storage, free trials for services like Apple Music and Apple TV, and the AppleCare+ extended warranty.
Infuriatingly for iOS users, the only way to disable these promos is to either let them expire — which in many cases could take weeks or even months, leaving a persistent notification badge on the Settings app in the meantime — or pay for the service being offered. There is not always a “dismiss” button to shoo them away for good, and when there is, some people have reported that it doesn’t seem to work.
Many people have taken to social media to vent their frustrations with Apple’s actions. “I’m feeling like this is nearly on-par with the ens***ification that Microsoft introduced with Start menu ads,” said one aggravated user. “I wish Apple would just stop that crap,” stated another. Many other people have taken to Reddit to express their exasperation, suggesting that the discontent is widespread.
Some of these ads and offers — such as the one for Apple Music — appear after you’ve bought a new Apple product. With the company launching the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro range recently, it’s perhaps unsurprising that we’re seeing a sudden influx of posts flush with irritation and indignation.
Apple’s services push
On the face of it, Apple’s decision to include promotions like this in its operating system might seem like a strange one. After all, Apple has long positioned itself as a premium company where the user experience is paramount. From that viewpoint, repeatedly attempting to prod customers towards even more of the company’s products might seem cheap, even distasteful. And when you’ve just shelled out a record fee for an iPhone after Apple’s painful price rises, that can just feel like nickel and diming.
But Apple has been putting increasing emphasis on its services in recent years, of which products like iCloud+, Apple Music, Apple TV and AppleCare+ are all a part. With limited room for growth in the smartphone market, the company is turning to areas where it thinks it can make more progress.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
And unfortunately for users, that means more ads like this on their devices. While they are far from the most obnoxious ads around, the fact that many cannot be dismissed is clearly rubbing users the wrong way — as is the fact that the promos even exist at all in an Apple product.
There is also the possibility that at least some of these adverts are appearing due to a bug. The iCloud+ one in particular has drawn comments from users who are already subscribed to iCloud+ and thus, one would think, should not need to see any ads like this. Time will tell how that plays out and whether Apple fixes this ‘bug’ or leaves the ads in place. If the latter transpires, it would suggest that they are not appearing erroneously.
With Apple’s services push showing no signs of slowing down and further ads supposedly planned for the likes of the firm’s Visual Intelligence system, don’t expect Apple to have a change of heart any time soon.

articles.title: Motorola Signature 27 : la marque de Lenovo tease un smartphone qui ne fait rien comme les autres
articles.text:
Motorola Signature 27 : la marque de Lenovo tease un smartphone qui ne fait rien comme les autres
Motorola prépare un nouveau smartphone premium qui entend clairement se faire remarquer. Entre ambitions photo, design atypique et partenariat audio prestigieux, le Signature 27 pourrait devenir l’un de ses flagships les plus ambitieux.
Quelques mois après un premier modèle Signature lancé début 2026, Motorola accélère déjà. Le constructeur profite du Snapdragon Summit de Qualcomm pour mettre en avant son Signature 27, clairement pensé pour jouer dans la cour des modèles les plus huppés.
Motorola Signature
Quatre caméras et un dos qui ne ressemble à aucun autre
À l’arrière, Motorola installe un large bloc asymétrique avec quatre modules photo et un flash répartis sur deux rangées. La composition exacte reste à confirmer, mais les teasers suggèrent un ultra grand-angle, un capteur principal Sony de 200 mégapixels, un téléobjectif classique et un module périscopique.
Le capteur principal pourrait être le Sony LYTIA 901, un grand modèle de 1/1,12 pouce avec des pixels de 0,7 µm. Motorola confirme en revanche un zoom pouvant atteindre x100 et la compatibilité Dolby Vision pour la vidéo.
Le design tranche aussi avec les dos en verre habituels. La coque adopte en effet une texture évoquant le textile ou le cuir végétal. Deux coloris Pantone sont déjà connus : vert olive et gris foncé.
Exceptional design. Exceptional sound.
Motorola and @BangOlufsen are proud to announce a new global partnership, bringing Audio by Bang & Olufsen to Motorola’s premium device portfolio.
Combining expertise in innovation, design and sound to create more meaningful experiences.… pic.twitter.com/24feX1ILdE
Bang & Olufsen, Snapdragon… et GrapheneOS ?
Motorola change également de partenaire audio. Bose, associé au premier Signature, laisse la place à Bang & Olufsen dans le cadre d’un accord mondial pluriannuel. Le Signature 27 inaugurera cette collaboration avec un réglage sonore spécifique, des modes dédiés et deux haut-parleurs stéréo placés en haut et en bas du terminal.
Si la marque de Lenovo garde encore le nom du processeur secret, sa présentation au Snapdragon Summit laisse toutefois attendre une puce Qualcomm haut de gamme de nouvelle génération, probablement issue de la famille Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6.
La surprise pourrait surtout venir de GrapheneOS. Le projet a indiqué que son premier smartphone Motorola compatible serait le successeur du Signature. Ce modèle pourrait donc devenir le premier non-Pixel officiellement pris en charge par ce système Android axé sur la sécurité et la confidentialité.
Reste à connaître le reste de sa fiche technique, ainsi que le prix — sans aucun doute élevé — et la date de sortie. Motorola a déjà teasé l’appareil aux États-Unis et en Europe, tandis que ses antennes au Brésil et en Inde participent aussi à la campagne, signe d’un lancement international probable.
